properties.formattedContent:
Question: vaccines that eradicated diseases

Answer: Vaccines have successfully eradicated two major infectious diseases::
- Smallpox: Eradicated globally in 1980.
- Polio: Nearly eradicated worldwide, with only a few cases remaining in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Other diseases that have been significantly reduced or eliminated in many parts of the world due to vaccination include:
Measles, Mumps, Rubella, Chickenpox, Diphtheria, Tetanus, Pertussis (whooping cough), and Hepatitis B.

0.fact: Vaccines have successfully eradicated two major infectious diseases:: - Smallpox: Eradicated globally in 1980.
0.explanation: Smallpox is the only human disease that has been officially eradicated globally, with the World Health Organization declaring its eradication in 1980. No cases have been reported since 1977.

1.fact: Polio: Nearly eradicated worldwide, with only a few cases remaining in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
1.explanation: Polio has not been fully eradicated but is close, with endemic transmission now limited to a few countries, primarily Afghanistan and Pakistan. Global vaccination efforts have drastically reduced cases worldwide.

2.fact: Other diseases that have been significantly reduced or eliminated in many parts of the world due to vaccination include: Measles, Mumps, Rubella, Chickenpox, Diphtheria, Tetanus, Pertussis (whooping cough), and Hepatitis B.
2.explanation: Vaccination programs have led to significant reductions or elimination of these diseases in many regions. Measles, mumps, rubella, chickenpox, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, and hepatitis B have all seen dramatic declines in incidence due to widespread immunization.
